skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray with complete opacification of a hemithorax to determine the underlying etiology based on mediastinal position and border morphology.
steps: Assess the direction of the mediastinal shift relative to the opacity: ipsilateral shift indicates volume loss (e.g., atelectasis), while contralateral shift indicates a space-occupying process (e.g., massive effusion, large mass, or tension pneumothorax).

Examine the medial border of the opacity: a convex border bulging into the mediastinum suggests a solid mass or loculated collection pushing structures away, whereas a concave or straight border (meniscus) is more typical of free-flowing fluid.

Differentiate between massive effusion and large mass by combining these findings: contralateral shift with a convex medial border strongly favors a large pleural-based mass over simple effusion or atelectasis.
